metadata.description: Open any DSH sidebar file, including HTML/PDF/images whose built-in preview fails, in the system default browser — one click from a tab chip's context menu.

ault browser — one click from a tab chip's context menu.
# dsh-plugin-open-in-browser

A community DSH plugin that opens a Sidebar file in the **system default browser**
instead of the in

SH plugin that opens a Sidebar file in the **system default browser**
instead of the in-app preview.
Two entry points ship in one plugin:
| Seat | Where it shows | What it needs from the Host |
| `sidebar.right.tab.document.unpreviewable` | "Cannot preview this file" empty state | the file's H

ost path (`absolutePath`) |
| `sidebar.right.tab.menu.item` | Right-click menu of a Sidebar **tab ch
ip** | only the tab's `contentId` (`dsh-resource://file/session/…`) |

There is deliberately **no** `sidebar.right.tab.document.actions` seat. When the
preview renders a f

ile, the header already carries the preview's own controls, and a
second "open in browser" button ne

xt to them earns nothing; the tab-chip menu is one
right-click away and works for every tab. That me

nu seat is also what makes the
plugin useful for a tab whose preview **fails**: the built-in preview

only renders
the document seats once its Host metadata read succeeds, so a tab showing an error
(fo

r example `HTTP 405` from a third-party previewer) has no `absolutePath`. The tab
menu still has the

tab's resource address, which is enough to resolve, verify, and
open the file.
## Install

The package ships prebuilt artifacts (`dist/`), so installing needs no build step
and no runtime dep

age ships prebuilt artifacts (`dist/`), so installing needs no build step
and no runtime dependency.

**From npm** — published as
`dsh-plugin-open-in-browser`:

1. Open DSH → **插件 → 添加插件**.
2. Enter the package name `dsh-plugin-open-in-browser`.
3. Fully quit a
nd reopen DSH so the new Host half and client artifact load.
The same target works from the plugin tooling:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**From a local checkout or a GitHub clone** (the clone already contains `dist/`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**Requirements**: the DSH desktop app (the Host must be able to launch a native
application); Node ≥

20 only when building from source. A remote/SSH deployment has
no desktop browser to launch, so the

control reports that instead of failing
silently.
[该节后续省略]
## Why

The built-in preview renders HTML inside a sandboxed `iframe` (`srcDoc`/blob). Pages
that depend on

`fetch`, modules, absolute paths, service workers, or a real origin
show up blank — and files the pr

eview cannot render at all show an empty state. The
fastest escape hatch is the OS: hand the file to

the default browser, which resolves
relative assets and origin-dependent APIs normally.
### Why no `src/main/`, `src/preload/`, `src/renderer/`?

Those are the layers of an **Electron application**. A DSH plugin is a Cordis
bundle, not an Electro

n app: it never reaches the Electron main process and DSH
exposes no preload/`contextBridge` bridge
to plugins. The equivalent split is:
| Electron app layer | This plugin |
| main process (Node) | `src/index.ts` + `src/browser.ts` — the Host half, running inside DSH's Host

process |
| preload / contextBridge | the Host route `POST /dsh-plugin-open-in-browser/open` (with

DSH's `session.openWorkspacePath` Remote as the fallback) |
| renderer injection | `src/client.ts` —
the browser artifact loaded through `window.__ModuleLoader__` |

`security.ts` is shared by both halves on purpose: the browser half validates
before calling, and th

e Host validates again before launching. Splitting it into
a "main" copy would let the two gates dri

lidates again before launching. Splitting it into
a "main" copy would let the two gates drift apart.
## Security notes

- The route is fenced on three layers: the Host web server's own authentication, a
same-origin `Orig

in` check (`dsh-app://app` or the serving `Host`; absent `Origin`
is a local client such as curl), a

nd a bounded JSON body (`16 KiB`,
`content-type: application/json` required). It can only ever open

a **file** path
that passes validation, never accept a command.
- The browser half validates before

calling: the path must be absolute, must not
contain `.`/`..`, UNC or device-namespace paths, contro

l characters, or reserved
device names, and its extension must be on the browser-safe whitelist.
- A

ddress-based requests are resolved against the Session's live `header.cwd`, then
passed through the

same gate **and** an injected `realpath`; a symlink that leaves
the workspace is rejected (`symlink-

escape`), as is an unknown Session
(`session-unavailable`) rather than guessing a root.
- Containmen

t against a workspace root is only possible where a root is known; on the
document seats the slot on

ly supplies the absolute path, so the Host mapping check
of the Remote (and of the preview itself) r
emains the authoritative fence there.
## Limitations

- No file-tree right-click menu. The slot catalog exposes no file-node context-menu
slot (only `side

bar.right.tab.files.actions`, a toolbar that receives the displayed
workspace directory), and the sh

ipped Files tree has no context menu of its own.
Adding one would require shipping a replacement fil

e tree (what
`dsh-better-sidebar` does).
- The empty-state button only appears once the preview has

metadata for the file
(`absolutePath`); a tab whose preview fails is covered by the tab-chip menu se

at.
- The preview header has no button at all by design (see above); if you want one back,
re-regist

er `sidebar.right.tab.document.actions` in `src/client.ts`.
- A profile restart is required after re

building, because the client artifact is
cached by the module loader.
- The whitelist is deliberatel

y small; extend `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS` if you want
more types opened externally.
## Security

The plugin adds a process-launch capability, so it ships with a written threat
model: the single Hos

t route, the fences around it, the path gate, and what is
explicitly out of scope. See docs/SECURITY

ute, the fences around it, the path gate, and what is
explicitly out of scope. See docs/SECURITY.md.

To report a vulnerability, use GitHub's private advisory form (Security tab) rather
than a public is

eport a vulnerability, use GitHub's private advisory form (Security tab) rather
than a public issue.
